decisive_items: systemic chemotherapy: paclitaxel and bevacizumab administered for 63 and 36 days before presentation, respectively, each followed the next day by cisplatin
cholangiography via the drainage tube revealed strictures and dilatations with irregular wall contours in the intrahepatic bile ducts of both lobes
Biopsy of the common bile duct showed no malignant cells and only modest infiltration of neutrophils; bile cytology was also negative for malignancy
response.rationale: The temporal link to chemotherapy, cholestatic liver enzyme pattern, and cholangiographic features of intrahepatic bile-duct strictures with dilatation and irregular contours, without malignancy, best fits chemotherapy-associated sclerosing cholangitis. Drug-induced cholestasis explains the exposure and liver enzymes but not the sclerosing bile-duct changes.

rejected.why: Cholangitis is nonspecific here; there is only modest neutrophil infiltration and no definite infectious/inflammatory evidence to explain the cholangiographic strictures.
Vanishing bile duct syndrome is a ductopenic histologic entity, whereas this case radiologically shows strictures, thickening, and dilatations rather than bile duct loss.
Drug-induced cholestasis accounts for chemotherapy exposure and liver enzyme elevation but does not explain the structural bile-duct stricturing and duct-wall thickening on imaging.
